text: Maybe the shop is open.
version_A: The shop is likely open near the station.
version_B: The shop is open near the station.
note: Add near the station.

text: Are we having lunch at the cafe?
version_A: The café serves lunch near the station.
version_B: Does the café serve lunch near the station?
note: Asks about our lunch rather than the cafe serving lunch.

text: Is the clinic open now?
version_A: The clinic opens at nine on Monday.
version_B: Does the clinic open at nine on Monday?
note: Asks about now instead of opening at nine on Monday.

text: I must walk the dog now.
version_A: The dog may need a walk before dinner.
version_B: The dog needs a walk before dinner.
note: Assigns the walk to me and changes before dinner to now.

text: The bus arrives now.
version_A: The bus may arrive near the library.
version_B: The bus arrives near the library.
note: Replace now with near the library.

text: I want to get off the bus at the next stop.
version_A: The bus stops beside the library.
version_B: Does the bus stop beside the library?
note: Introduces my wish to get off the bus.

text: The soup is definitely warm.
version_A: The soup is probably warm in the kitchen.
version_B: The soup is warm in the kitchen.
note: Adds definite certainty and omits the kitchen.

text: Tell you to turn the lamp off.
version_A: You turn the lamp off after dinner.
version_B: Turn the lamp off after dinner.
note: Reporting fragment; neither statement nor complete instruction.

text: The game is starting.
version_A: The game might start after the break.
version_B: The game starts after the break.
note: Restore after the break rather than starting now.

text: The nurse is going to bandage me.
version_A: The nurse checks the bandage after lunch.
version_B: Does the nurse check the bandage after lunch?
note: Changes checking a bandage into bandaging me.

text: Please check my bank balance.
version_A: Could you check the bank balance today?
version_B: Can you check the bank balance today?
note: Add today.

text: I must finish the report.
version_A: I finished the report at school on Monday.
version_B: I will finish the report at school on Friday.
note: Obligation without the stated Friday plan or school location.

text: The bus will arrive.
version_A: The bus arrived at the station earlier.
version_B: The bus will arrive at the station soon.
note: Add at the station soon.

text: Please knock on the room.
version_A: Would you knock before entering my room at home?
version_B: Can you knock before entering my room at home?
note: Knock on my door before entering my room at home.

text: Can you please give me some space?
version_A: I asked for more space at work last week.
version_B: I am asking for more space at work now.
note: A direct request for space omits the workplace.

text: I like the lower music.
version_A: Please lower the music in the car.
version_B: Lower the music in the car.
note: Preference instead of a request to lower the music.

text: I want to pay the bill later.
version_A: I paid the phone bill last week.
version_B: I will pay the phone bill next week.
note: Desire to pay later is not the plan to pay next week.

text: Please pass the bread.
version_A: Please pass the bread at dinner.
version_B: Pass the bread at dinner.
note: Add at dinner.

text: I invite you to come over.
version_A: Could you invite my cousin to the picnic?
version_B: Can you invite my cousin to the picnic?
note: Changes who invites whom and omits my cousin and picnic.

text: Let's meet at the cafe.
version_A: We met at the cafe downtown yesterday.
version_B: We will meet at the cafe downtown tomorrow.
note: Suggestion without the intended downtown location or tomorrow.

text: I want to pay the bill.
version_A: I pay the bill from my account.
version_B: The bank pays the bill from my account.
note: Wishing to pay is not paying from my account.

text: Tell clinic about walk-ins.
version_A: The clinic takes walk-ins on Monday.
version_B: Does the clinic take walk-ins on Monday?
note: Instruction to tell the clinic, not whether walk-ins are accepted.

text: Please save a seat.
version_A: My friend saves a seat at the game.
version_B: I save a seat at the game.
note: Asks the listener to save a seat, neither specified doer.

text: I tell you the pharmacy is open.
version_A: The pharmacy opens on Sunday.
version_B: Does the pharmacy open on Sunday?
note: Remove the reporting frame and add on Sunday.

text: Leave the package.
version_A: You leave the package by the door.
version_B: Leave the package by the door.
note: Add by the door.

text: I carry an inhaler.
version_A: The nurse carries my inhaler in the bag.
version_B: I carry my inhaler in the bag.
note: Use my inhaler in the bag.

text: They practice guitar.
version_A: I practice guitar in the living room.
version_B: My brother practices guitar in the living room.
note: Unspecified they instead of my brother; living room omitted.

text: I want to start the music
version_A: The music starts after the break.
version_B: Does the music start after the break?
note: My wish to start the music replaces the scheduled start.

text: They sent the report.
version_A: You send the report before lunch today.
version_B: The manager sends the report before lunch today.
note: Past action with an unnamed doer instead of the manager before lunch.

text: Please turn the lamp off.
version_A: You turn the lamp off at bedtime.
version_B: Turn the lamp off at bedtime.
note: Restore at bedtime; remove please for the original wording.

text: Let's go to the park for a picnic now.
version_A: The picnic starts at noon in the park.
version_B: Does the picnic start at noon in the park?
note: Suggestion to go now instead of a noon start.

text: Please bring the prescription.
version_A: Bring my prescription from the pharmacy.
version_B: Please bring my prescription from the pharmacy.
note: Add my and from the pharmacy.

text: The hallway lights are bright.
version_A: The hallway lights are too bright today.
version_B: Are the hallway lights too bright today?
note: Add too and today to recover the complaint.

text: Please keep the office door closed.
version_A: Keep the office door closed during lunch.
version_B: Please keep the office door closed during lunch.
note: Add during lunch.

text: I will tell the neighbor to feed the cat.
version_A: The neighbor feeds our cat this morning.
version_B: Does the neighbor feed our cat this morning?
note: A plan to instruct the neighbor replaces a claim about feeding.

text: I need to check the rent payment.
version_A: Check the rent payment on Tuesday.
version_B: Please check the rent payment on Tuesday.
note: A personal need rather than a request to another person.

text: Does my cousin enter the room?
version_A: Your cousin can enter my room now.
version_B: Can your cousin enter my room now?
note: Changes your cousin to my cousin and permission to usual action.

text: I want to collect medicine.
version_A: Collect my medicine from the clinic.
version_B: Please collect my medicine from the clinic.
note: Makes me the collector rather than asking the listener.

text: I need to book a taxi at the station.
version_A: Book the morning taxi to the station.
version_B: Please book the morning taxi to the station.
note: A personal need, with taxi at rather than to the station.

text: [TELL] The chess club meets now.
version_A: The chess club meets at the center.
version_B: Does the chess club meet at the center?
note: Remove the chip and replace now with at the center.

text: I don't have cream for breakfast.
version_A: I use the cream after breakfast.
version_B: I do not use the cream after breakfast.
note: Cream for breakfast instead of using cream after breakfast.

text: The ramp is sure open.
version_A: The ramp is perhaps open near the entrance.
version_B: The ramp is open near the entrance.
note: Use the ramp is open near the entrance without sure.

text: I want to play music on the guitar.
version_A: The guitar might stay in the music room.
version_B: The guitar stays in the music room.
note: Playing guitar instead of its staying in the music room.

text: I want to play the band.
version_A: The band plays at the park tonight.
version_B: The band does not play at the park tonight.
note: My wish to play a band instead of the band playing tonight.

text: My sister is in the garden.
version_A: My sister visits the garden on Sunday.
version_B: My sister does not visit the garden on Sunday.
note: Current location instead of a Sunday visit.

text: I am sure I need to wait for the taxi.
version_A: The taxi may wait outside the main gate.
version_B: The taxi waits outside the main gate.
note: I wait for the taxi rather than the taxi waiting at the gate.

text: I must pay the bank fee.
version_A: The bank might waive the monthly fee.
version_B: The bank waives the monthly fee.
note: Paying a fee rather than the bank waiving it.

text: Yes, quiet music.
version_A: I ask for quiet in the music room.
version_B: I do not ask for quiet in the music room.
note: Quiet music is not a request for quiet in the music room.

text: You have a friend in the fifth seat.
version_A: My friend saves a seat near the stage.
version_B: My friend does not save a seat near the stage.
note: Invents a fifth seat instead of saving a seat near the stage.

text: Let's start the game.
version_A: The game might start beside the river.
version_B: The game starts beside the river.
note: Suggestion to start instead of a statement about starting.

text: Check the gate.
version_A: The guard checked the gate this morning.
version_B: The guard checks the gate now.
note: Listener instruction instead of a statement about the guard.

text: I will call the clinic later.
version_A: The nurse called the clinic yesterday.
version_B: The nurse will call the clinic tomorrow.
note: Speaker replaces the nurse and tomorrow becomes later.

text: I went to the park and took a taxi.
version_A: The driver parked the taxi by the hotel.
version_B: The driver will park the taxi by the hotel later.
note: Park becomes a place and the taxi action changes.

text: I want to play guitar music.
version_A: I played guitar in the music room last night.
version_B: I will play guitar in the music room tonight.
note: Desire to play omits the stated room and tonight.

text: I showed you friend photos from the past.
version_A: My friend brought photos to the party last night.
version_B: My friend brings photos to the party tonight.
note: I showed old photos instead of my friend bringing them to a party.

text: I need to look at the therapist's chart.
version_A: The therapist showed me the chart last visit.
version_B: The therapist will show me the chart next visit.
note: My need to look replaces the therapist showing it.

text: I booked the room in the past.
version_A: We booked the room last week.
version_B: We will book the room next week.
note: I replaces we and the date last week is lost.

text: My sister is in the garden.
version_A: My sister visited our garden last Sunday.
version_B: My sister will visit our garden next Sunday.
note: Being there now is not the specified Sunday visit.

text: I’ll pay the bill at the office later.
version_A: I paid the bill at the office window yesterday.
version_B: I will pay the bill at the office window tomorrow.
note: Use at the office window tomorrow.

text: I will pay the bill.
version_A: I can pay the utility bill this week.
version_B: I can't pay the utility bill this week.
note: A commitment to pay differs from ability this week.

text: I want to lower the music.
version_A: I lower the music in the car.
version_B: You lower the music in the car.
note: Wishing to lower the music is not lowering it in the car.

text: I want to visit my sister.
version_A: I want to visit my sister after work.
version_B: I don't want to visit my sister after work.
note: Restore after work.

text: I explain my schedule.
version_A: The therapist explains the schedule in the office.
version_B: I explain the schedule in the office.
note: Use the schedule in the office.

text: I want the door.
version_A: I want the door closed at night.
version_B: I don't want the door closed at night.
note: Wanting the door itself leaves out closed at night.

text: I want to cook rice.
version_A: Dad cooks rice for dinner at home.
version_B: I cook rice for dinner at home.
note: Wish to cook differs from cooking rice for dinner at home.

text: I am not going to ride to the clinic.
version_A: I need a ride to the clinic tomorrow.
version_B: I don't need a ride to the clinic tomorrow.
note: Not going differs from not needing a ride tomorrow.

text: I invite Sam.
version_A: My friend invites Sam to the picnic this weekend.
version_B: I invite Sam to the picnic this weekend.
note: Add to the picnic this weekend.

text: I want to play chess.
version_A: My cousin plays chess at home after dinner.
version_B: I play chess at home after dinner.
note: Wishing to play omits the actual event and its place and time.

text: I did not finish the report.
version_A: I have time to finish the report today.
version_B: I don't have time to finish the report today.
note: Failure to finish in the past differs from lacking time today.

text: I was a driver at the hotel.
version_A: The driver waited beside the hotel yesterday.
version_B: The driver waits beside the hotel now.
note: Changes the driver waiting into me being a driver.

text: Please turn the light off.
version_A: You turn the hallway light off at bedtime.
version_B: Turn the hallway light off at bedtime.
note: Restore hallway and at bedtime; please is extra.

text: The band plays now.
version_A: The band plays at the park tonight.
version_B: Does the band play at the park tonight?
note: Replace now with at the park tonight.

text: I have photos of my friend.
version_A: My friend brought photos to the café last night.
version_B: My friend will bring photos to the café tonight.
note: Having photos of my friend is not my friend bringing photos.

text: Please wait for the dog.
version_A: The dog waits outside the kitchen door.
version_B: Does the dog wait outside the kitchen door?
note: Asks me to wait instead of describing the dog waiting.

text: I used the ramp entrance in the past.
version_A: The therapist checked the ramp at the entrance.
version_B: The therapist will check the ramp at the entrance later.
note: The therapist checking becomes me using the ramp.

text: I will lock the door later.
version_A: I locked the front door after dinner.
version_B: I will lock the front door after dinner.
note: Restore front door and after dinner.

text: The cafe is now closed.
version_A: The café closes before the station shuts.
version_B: Does the café close before the station shuts?
note: Describes a closed cafe now, rather than its closing time relative to the station.

text: I cooked vegetables in the past.
version_A: I cooked the vegetables in the kitchen yesterday.
version_B: I will cook the vegetables in the kitchen tomorrow.
note: Restore in the kitchen yesterday.

text: Do you have class today?
version_A: The class meets in the upstairs room.
version_B: Does the class meet in the upstairs room?
note: Asks about having class today, not where the class meets.

text: I’ll ask for an interpreter later.
version_A: I asked for an interpreter at the clinic yesterday.
version_B: I will ask for an interpreter at the clinic tomorrow.
note: Restore at the clinic tomorrow.

text: I want to take medicine.
version_A: I take medicine with breakfast.
version_B: I don't take medicine with breakfast.
note: Wanting medicine is different from taking it with breakfast.

text: I need captions.
version_A: I need captions during the meeting.
version_B: I don't need captions during the meeting.
note: Add during the meeting.

text: Please close the door.
version_A: I closed the bedroom door before bed last night.
version_B: I will close the bedroom door before bed tonight.
note: Changes my past or future action into a request to someone else.

text: I waited for the bus.
version_A: I waited for the bus at the station yesterday.
version_B: I am waiting for the bus at the station now.
note: Add at the station yesterday.

text: I will finish the report.
version_A: I finished the report before lunch.
version_B: I didn't finish the report before lunch.
note: A future completion replaces whether I finished before lunch.

text: I don’t want a bright light.
version_A: The bright light bothers me in the bedroom.
version_B: The bright light doesn't bother me in the bedroom.
note: Not wanting a light differs from whether it bothers me.

text: The soup is salty now.
version_A: The soup tasted salty at lunch yesterday.
version_B: The soup tastes salty at lunch today.
note: Restore at lunch today.

text: I want quiet.
version_A: I want a quiet weekend at home.
version_B: I don't want a quiet weekend at home.
note: Add a weekend at home.

text: I will go to the train platform now.
version_A: My train left the platform ten minutes ago.
version_B: My train will leave the platform in ten minutes.
note: Going to the platform is different from the train leaving.

text: I want to go to the park with my family.
version_A: The family might meet at the park tonight.
version_B: The family meets at the park tonight.
note: My wish to go replaces whether the family meets there tonight.

text: I need a taxi to the hotel.
version_A: The driver parked the taxi beside the hotel.
version_B: The driver will park the taxi beside the hotel later.
note: My need for a taxi replaces the driver parking it.

text: The clinic is open.
version_A: The clinic may open on Sunday.
version_B: The clinic opens on Sunday.
note: Add on Sunday and use opens.

text: The screen was in the room.
version_A: The screen flashed in the quiet room last night.
version_B: The screen flashes in the quiet room now.
note: Only locates the screen, with no flashing.

text: We need to clear the ramp.
version_A: Perhaps the ramp is clear beside the entrance.
version_B: The ramp is clear beside the entrance.
note: Says we need to clear it rather than whether it is already clear.

text: I had lunch in the kitchen.
version_A: I prepared lunch in the kitchen this morning.
version_B: I will prepare lunch in the kitchen tomorrow morning.
note: Eating lunch replaces preparing it and loses the date.

text: I had soup in the dining room.
version_A: We served soup in the dining room yesterday.
version_B: We serve soup in the dining room now.
note: Eating soup replaces serving it.

text: I am sure the chef made the soup.
version_A: I guess the chef prepared soup for dinner.
version_B: The chef prepared soup for dinner.
note: Remove I am sure and restore for dinner.

text: I will show them photos of my friend later.
version_A: My friend brought photos to the café last night.
version_B: My friend brings photos to the café tonight.
note: Showing photos of my friend replaces my friend bringing photos.

text: My sister is in the garden.
version_A: My sister probably visits the garden on Friday.
version_B: My sister visits the garden on Friday.
note: Change to My sister visits the garden on Friday.
